text: If $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+x}+\sqrt{1+x}}\mathrm{d}x=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}\sqrt{2}+\mathrm{c}\sqrt{3}$, where $\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c}$ are rational numbers, then $2\mathrm{a}+3\mathrm{b}-4\mathrm{c}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \int\limits _{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3+x}+\sqrt{1+x}}dx=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\dfrac{\sqrt{3+x}-\sqrt{1+x}}{(3+x)-(1+x)}dx \\ \dfrac{1}{2}\left [\int\limits _{0}^{1}\sqrt{3+x}dx-\int\limits _{0}^{1}(\sqrt{1+x})dx\right ] \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{2}\left [2\dfrac{(3+x)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}-\dfrac{2(1+x)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}\right ]_{0}^{1} \\ \dfrac{1}{2}\left [\dfrac{2}{3}(8-3\sqrt{3})-\dfrac{2}{3}\left (2^{\frac{3}{2}}-1\right )\right ] \\ \dfrac{1}{3}[8-3\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{2}+1] \\ =3-\sqrt{3}-\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}=a+b\sqrt{2}+c\sqrt{3} \\ a=3,b=-\dfrac{2}{3},c=-1 \\ 2a+3b-4c=6-2+4=8 \end{array}$

text:
Let $S=\{1,2,3,\ldots ,10\}$. Suppose $M$ is the set of all the subsets of $S$, then the relation 

$\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}):\mathrm{A}\cap \mathrm{B}\neq 𝜙;\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\in \mathrm{M}\}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$M$ is the set of all subsets of $S$, so $𝜙\in M$. Since $𝜙\cap 𝜙=𝜙$, $(𝜙,𝜙)\notin R$; hence $R$ is not reflexive.

If $A\cap B\neq 𝜙$, then $B\cap A=A\cap B\neq 𝜙$; hence $R$ is symmetric.

For $A=\{1\}$, $B=\{1,2\}$, $C=\{2\}$: $A\cap B=\{1\}\neq 𝜙$ and $B\cap C=\{2\}\neq 𝜙$, but $A\cap C=𝜙$. So $(A,B)\in R$ and $(B,C)\in R$ while $(A,C)\notin R$; hence $R$ is not transitive.

Thus $R$ is symmetric only.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: Let $x=x(\mathrm{t})$ and $y=y(\mathrm{t})$ be solutions of the differential equations $\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{a}x=0$ and $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{by}=0$ respectively, $\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b}\in 𝐑$. Given that $x(0)=2;y(0)=1$ and $3y(1)=2x(1)$, the value of $\mathrm{t}$, for which $x(\mathrm{t})=y(\mathrm{t})$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{ax}=0 \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}}=-\mathrm{adt} \\ \int \dfrac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}}=-\mathrm{a}\int \mathrm{dt} \\ \ln |\mathrm{x}|=-\mathrm{at}+\mathrm{c} \\ \mathrm{at}\mathrm{t}=0,\mathrm{x}=2 \\ \ln 2=0+\mathrm{c} \\ \ln \mathrm{x}=-\mathrm{at}+\ln 2 \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{x}}{2}=\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{at}} \\ \mathrm{x}=2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{at}}\text{.... (i)} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{dy}{dt}+by=0 \\ \dfrac{dy}{y}=-bdt \\ \ln |y|=-bt+λ \\ t=0,y=1 \\ 0=0+λ \\ y=e^{-bt}\text{..... (ii)} \end{array}$

According to question

$\begin{array}{l} 3\mathrm{y}(1)=2\mathrm{x}(1) \\ 3\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{b}}=2\left (2\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{a}}\right ) \\ \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}}=\dfrac{4}{3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{For}x(t)=y(t) \\ \begin{array}{l} 2\mathrm{e}^{-at}=e^{-bt} \\ 2=e^{(a-b)t} \\ 2=\left (\frac{4}{3}\right )^{t} \\ \log _{\frac{4}{3}}2=t \end{array} \end{array}$

text: The length of the chord of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{25}+\frac{y^{2}}{16}=1$, whose mid point is $\left (1,\frac{2}{5}\right )$, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The chord with mid-point $\left (1,\frac{2}{5}\right )$ is given by $T=S_{1}$:

$\frac{x}{25}+\frac{2y}{5\times 16}=\frac{1}{25}+\frac{4}{25\times 16}\Rightarrow \frac{x}{25}+\frac{y}{40}=\frac{1}{20}\Rightarrow 8x+5y=10$

Substituting $y=\dfrac{10-8x}{5}$ in $16x^{2}+25y^{2}=400$:

$16x^{2}+(10-8x)^{2}=400\Rightarrow 80x^{2}-160x-300=0\Rightarrow 4x^{2}-8x-15=0$

So $x_{1}+x_{2}=2$ and $x_{1}x_{2}=-\dfrac{15}{4}$, giving $(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2}=(x_{1}+x_{2})^{2}-4x_{1}x_{2}=4+15=19$.

The slope of the chord is $-\dfrac{8}{5}$, so $(y_{1}-y_{2})^{2}=\dfrac{64}{25}(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2}$ and

$\text{Length}=\sqrt{(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2}\left (1+\frac{64}{25}\right )}=\sqrt{19\times \frac{89}{25}}=\frac{\sqrt{1691}}{5}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text:
Consider the function.

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{\mathrm{a}\left (7x-12-x^{2}\right )}{\mathrm{b}|x^{2}-7x+12|} & ,x<3 \\  \\ 2^{\frac{\sin (x-3)}{x-[x]}} & ,x>3 \\  \\ \mathrm{b} & ,x=3, \end{array} \right.$

where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. If $\mathrm{S}$ denotes the set of all ordered pairs (a, b) such that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=3$, then the number of elements in $\mathrm{S}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(3^{-})=\frac{a}{b}\frac{\left (7x-12-x^{2}\right )}{|x^{2}-7x+12|}$ (for $f(x)$ to be cont.)

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(3^{-})=\frac{-\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{b}}\frac{(\mathrm{x}-3)(\mathrm{x}-4)}{(\mathrm{x}-3)(\mathrm{x}-4)};\mathrm{x}<3\Rightarrow \frac{-\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{b}}$

Hence $f(3^{-})=\frac{-a}{b}$

Then $f(3^{+})=2^{\lim _{x\to 3+}\left (\frac{\sin (x-3)}{x-3}\right )}=2$ and $f(3)=b$.

Hence $\mathrm{f}(3)=\mathrm{f}(3^{+})=\mathrm{f}(3^{-})$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=2=-\dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{b}} \\ \mathrm{b}=2,\mathrm{a}=-4 \end{array}$

Hence only 1 ordered pair $(-4,2)$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: If $\mathrm{a}=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+x^{4}}}-\sqrt{2}}{x^{4}}$ and $\mathrm{b}=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sin ^{2}x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}}$, then the value of $ab^{3}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} a= & \lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+x^{4}}}-\sqrt{2}}{x^{4}} \\ =\lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x^{4}}-1}{x^{4}\left (\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+x^{4}}}+\sqrt{2}\right )} \\ =\lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{x^{4}}{x^{4}\left (\sqrt{1+\sqrt{1+x^{4}}}+\sqrt{2}\right )\left (\sqrt{1+x^{4}}+1\right )} \end{array}$

Applying limit $\mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}$

$\begin{array}{l} b=\lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sin ^{2}x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}} \\ =\lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{\left (1-\cos ^{2}x\right )(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x})}{2-(1+\cos x)} \\ b=\lim _{x\to 0}(1+\cos x)(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}) \end{array}$

Applying limits $b=2(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2})=4\sqrt{2}$

Now, $ab^{3}=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}\times (4\sqrt{2})^{3}=32$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text:
Consider the matrix $f(x)=\left [\begin{array}{lll} \cos x & -\sin x & 0 \\ \sin x & \cos x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$.

Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $f(-x)$ is the inverse of the matrix $f(x)$.

Statement II : $f(x)f(y)=f(x+y)$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllllll} f(-x)=\left [\begin{array}{lll} \cos x & \sin x & 0 \\ -\sin x & \cos x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ f(x)\cdot f(-x)=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=I \end{array}$

Hence statement- I is correct

Now, checking statement II

$\begin{array}{lllllll} f(y)=\left [\begin{array}{lll} \cos y & -\sin y & 0 \\ \sin y & \cos y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ f(x)\cdot f(y)=\left [\begin{array}{lll} \cos (x+y) & -\sin (x+y) & 0 \\ \sin (x+y) & \cos (x+y) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ \Rightarrow f(x)\cdot f(y)=f(x+y) \end{array}$

Hence statement-II is also correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{x-4}{1}=\dfrac{y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z}{-3} \\ \dfrac{x-λ}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{4}=\dfrac{z-2}{-5} \end{array}$

the shortest distance between the lines

$=\left |\frac{\right |\begin{array}{lll} λ-4 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -5 \end{array}\left |}{\right |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -5 \end{array}\left |}\right |$

Sum of all possible values of $λ$ is $=8$

text: The portion of the line $4x+5y=20$ in the first quadrant is trisected by the lines $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ passing through the origin. The tangent of an angle between the lines $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
The line $4x+5y=20$ meets the axes at $(0,4)$ and $(5,0)$. The points dividing this segment in the ratios $1:2$ and $2:1$ (from $(0,4)$) are

$A=\left (\dfrac{1\cdot 5+2\cdot 0}{3},\dfrac{1\cdot 0+2\cdot 4}{3}\right )=\left (\dfrac{5}{3},\dfrac{8}{3}\right ),B=\left (\dfrac{2\cdot 5+1\cdot 0}{3},\dfrac{2\cdot 0+1\cdot 4}{3}\right )=\left (\dfrac{10}{3},\dfrac{4}{3}\right )$


[IMG]

$L_{1}=OA$ and $L_{2}=OB$ have slopes $m_{1}=\dfrac{8/3}{5/3}=\dfrac{8}{5}$ and $m_{2}=\dfrac{4/3}{10/3}=\dfrac{2}{5}$.

$\tan θ=\left |\dfrac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{1+m_{1}m_{2}}\right |=\dfrac{\frac{6}{5}}{1+\frac{16}{25}}=\dfrac{6}{5}\times \dfrac{25}{41}=\dfrac{30}{41}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{10}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{k}}=50 \\ \mathrm{a}_{1}+\mathrm{a}_{2}+\ldots +\mathrm{a}_{10}=50\text{.... (i)} \\ \sum\limits _{\forall \mathrm{k}<\mathrm{j}}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{j}}=1100\text{.... (ii)} \\ \text{If}\mathrm{a}_{1}+\mathrm{a}_{2}+\ldots +\mathrm{a}_{10}=50. \\ (\mathrm{a}_{1}+\mathrm{a}_{2}+\ldots +\mathrm{a}_{10})^{2}=2500 \\ \Rightarrow \sum\limits _{\mathrm{i}=1}^{10}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}+2\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}<\mathrm{j}}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{k}}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{j}}=2500 \\ \Rightarrow \sum\limits _{\mathrm{i}=1}^{10}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}=2500-2(1100) \\ \sum\limits _{\mathrm{i}=1}^{10}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}=300\text{, Standard deviation ‘}σ\text{’} \end{array}$

text: If A denotes the sum of all the coefficients in the expansion of $\left (1-3x+10x^{2}\right )^{\mathrm{n}}$ and B denotes the sum of all the coefficients in the expansion of $\left (1+x^{2}\right )^{n}$, then :

solution.body:
Sum of coefficients in the expansion of $\left (1-3\mathrm{x}+10\mathrm{x}^{2}\right )^{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{A}$

then $A=(1-3+10)^{n}=8^{n}$ (put $x=1$)

text:
If the solution of the differential equation 

$(2x+3y-2)\mathrm{d}x+(4x+6y-7)\mathrm{d}y=0,y(0)=3$, is 

$αx+βy+3\log _{e}|2x+3y-γ|=6$, then $α+2β+3γ$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put $2x+3y-2=t$, so $2+3\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dt}{dx}$ and $4x+6y-7=2t-3$. The equation gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{t}{2t-3}$, so

$\dfrac{dt}{dx}=2-\dfrac{3t}{2t-3}=\dfrac{t-6}{2t-3}$

Separating variables:

$\int \dfrac{2t-3}{t-6}dt=\int dx\Rightarrow \int \left (2+\dfrac{9}{t-6}\right )dt=x+c\Rightarrow 2t+9\ln |t-6|=x+c$

So $2(2x+3y-2)+9\ln |2x+3y-8|=x+c$. At $x=0$, $y=3$: $14+9\ln 1=c$, so $c=14$ and

$3x+6y+9\ln |2x+3y-8|=18\Rightarrow x+2y+3\ln |2x+3y-8|=6$

Comparing, $α=1$, $β=2$, $γ=8$, so $α+2β+3γ=1+4+24=29$.

Hence, the answer is 29.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

Let $x<y$

text: Let the area of the region $\left \{(x,y):x-2y+4⩾0,x+2y^{2}⩾0,x+4y^{2}\leq 8,y⩾0\right \}$ be $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}$, where $\mathrm{m}$ and $\mathrm{n}$ are coprime numbers. Then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $y\geq 0$ the region is $\max \left (2y-4,-2y^{2}\right )\leq x\leq 8-4y^{2}$.

The line $x=2y-4$ and the parabola $x=-2y^{2}$ meet where $2y^{2}+2y-4=0$, i.e. $y=1$; for $0\leq y\leq 1$ the left boundary is $x=-2y^{2}$, and for $y\geq 1$ it is $x=2y-4$.

The line meets $x=8-4y^{2}$ where $4y^{2}+2y-12=0$, i.e. $2y^{2}+y-6=0$, so $y=\dfrac{3}{2}$; for larger $y$ the region is empty.

$A=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left [(8-4y^{2})-(-2y^{2})\right ]dy+\int\limits _{1}^{3/2}\left [(8-4y^{2})-(2y-4)\right ]dy$

$A=\left [8y-\frac{2y^{3}}{3}\right ]_{0}^{1}+\left [12y-y^{2}-\frac{4y^{3}}{3}\right ]_{1}^{3/2}=\frac{22}{3}+\left (\frac{45}{4}-\frac{29}{3}\right )=\frac{22}{3}+\frac{19}{12}=\frac{107}{12}$

Since $107$ is prime, $m=107$, $n=12$ and $m+n=119$.

Hence, the answer is 119.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

$\mathrm{AB}_{1}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ],\mathrm{AB}_{2}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 2 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ],\mathrm{AB}_{3}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{A}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\mathrm{B}=[\mathrm{B}_{1},\mathrm{B}_{2},\mathrm{B}_{3}]$

$\mathrm{B}_{1}=\left [\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}_{1} \\ \mathrm{y}_{1} \\ \mathrm{z}_{1} \end{array}\right ],\mathrm{B}_{2}=\left [\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}_{2} \\ \mathrm{y}_{2} \\ \mathrm{z}_{2} \end{array}\right ],\mathrm{B}_{3}=\left [\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}_{3} \\ \mathrm{y}_{3} \\ \mathrm{z}_{3} \end{array}\right ]$

$\mathrm{AB}_{1}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}_{1} \\ \mathrm{y}_{1} \\ \mathrm{z}_{1} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \mathrm{x}_{1}=1,\mathrm{y}_{1}=-1,\mathrm{z}_{1}=-1 \\ \mathrm{AB}_{2}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}_{2} \\ \mathrm{y}_{2} \\ \mathrm{z}_{2} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 2 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ] \\ \mathrm{x}_{2}=2,\mathrm{y}_{2}=1,\mathrm{z}_{2}=-2 \\ \mathrm{AB}_{3}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}_{3} \\ \mathrm{y}_{3} \\ \mathrm{z}_{3} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ \mathrm{x}_{3}=2,\mathrm{y}_{3}=0,\mathrm{z}_{3}=-1 \\ \mathrm{B}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 \end{array}\right ] \\ α=|\mathrm{B}|=3 \\ β=1 \\ α^{3}+β^{3}=27+1=28 \end{array}$

text:
A fair die is tossed repeatedly until a six is obtained. Let $X$ denote the number of tosses required and let 

$a=P(X=3),b=P(X⩾3)$ and $c=P(X⩾6|X>3)$. Then $\frac{b+c}{a}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we need to compute the probabilities $a$, $b$, and $c$, and then plug those values into the expression $\frac{b+c}{a}$.

Let's begin by defining each of the variables:

$a=P(X=3)$: This is the probability that the first six appears on the third toss.

$b=P(X⩾3)$: This is the probability that the first six appears on the third toss or later.

$c=P(X⩾6|X>3)$: This is the probability that the first six appears on the sixth toss or later, given that it has not appeared in the first three tosses.

Since we're dealing with a fair die, each side has an equal probability of $\frac{1}{6}$ of landing face up. Let's find the probabilities step by step:

Calculating $a$:

The probability of rolling anything other than a six is $\frac{5}{6}$. So for the first six to show up exactly on the third roll, the sequence of rolls must be NN6, where N is anything but a six (i.e., the results of the first two rolls). Thus,

$a=P(X=3)=\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{6}\right )$

Calculating $b$:

For the first six to appear on the third roll or later, we can think of two cases: when the first six appears on the third roll (which we've already calculated, $a$), and when it appears after the third roll. To combine these probabilities, we can use the fact that $P(X⩾3)=1-P(X<3)$, where $P(X<3)$ is the probability that the first six appears on either the first or the second roll. So we calculate the latter first:

$P(X<3)=P(X=1)+P(X=2)$

$P(X<3)=\left (\frac{1}{6}\right )+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{6}\right )$

Thus,

$b=P(X⩾3)=1-P(X<3)=1-\left [\left (\frac{1}{6}\right )+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{6}\right )\right ]$

Calculating $c$:

This is the probability that the first six appears on or after the sixth roll, given that it hasn't appeared in the first three rolls. Since $X>3$, the first three outcomes must not be a six, which occurs with probability $\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{3}$. The subsequent outcomes until (and including) the fifth roll also must not be a six. So,

$c=P(X⩾6|X>3)=\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}$

Notice here, we did not include the probability of rolling a six, because we are looking for the probability that we have not yet rolled a six after the fifth roll.

Now we can calculate $a$, $b$, and $c$:

$a=\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}$

$b=1-\left [\left (\frac{1}{6}\right )+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{6}\right )\right ]$

$c=\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}$

Now we'll substitute to find $\frac{b+c}{a}$:

$\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{1-\left [\left (\frac{1}{6}\right )+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{6}\right )\right ]+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}}{\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}}$

Simplifying the numerator:

$1-\left [\left (\frac{1}{6}\right )+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{6}\right )\right ]+\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}$

$=1-\left [\frac{1}{6}+\frac{5}{36}\right ]+\frac{25}{36}$

$=1-\left [\frac{6}{36}+\frac{5}{36}\right ]+\frac{25}{36}$

$=1-\frac{11}{36}+\frac{25}{36}$

$=\frac{36}{36}-\frac{11}{36}+\frac{25}{36}$

$=\frac{50}{36}$

Now, substitute this back into the expression and solve:

$\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{\frac{50}{36}}{\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}}$

$\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{50}{36}\cdot \frac{6}{\left (\frac{5}{6}\right )^{2}}$

$\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{50\cdot 6}{25}$

$\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{300}{25}$

$\frac{b+c}{a}=12$

Therefore, $\frac{b+c}{a}=12$.
